description: The plot titled “BBQ” illustrates how accuracy varies with the number of demonstrations for four models. The x-axis is labeled “#Demonstrations,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 1500 with labeled ticks at 0, 250, 500, 750, 1000, 1250, and 1500. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and shows labeled ticks at 45, 50, and 55 (with the plotted values extending slightly above 55). The Squared-Exponential series is drawn as a dark navy solid line with circular markers, starting near 52 at 0 demonstrations, rising to about 54–55 by roughly 100 demonstrations, reaching about 56 around 250 demonstrations, and then staying near 56 through 1500 demonstrations with small fluctuations. The Tanh series is a medium-blue solid line with circular markers, beginning around 48 at 0 demonstrations and remaining close to 48–49 across the range, ending just under about 49 at 1500 demonstrations. The ELU series is a light purple solid line with circular markers, starting around 46 at 0 demonstrations and staying near 46–47 across all demonstration counts, ending around 46–47 at 1500 demonstrations. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B reference is shown as a magenta dashed horizontal line (no markers) positioned near 43 accuracy and remaining flat at that level across the full x-axis range.
caption_used: MC1 scores of model performance on the BBQ task as a function of the number of demonstrations, illustrating comparative accuracy trends. The line plot displays accuracy on the y-axis (ranging from 45 to 55) against the number of demonstrations on the x-axis (0 to 1500). The Squared Exponential model, represented by a dark blue line with circle markers, achieves an initial accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, rapidly climbing to 56 by 250 demonstrations before stabilizing around 55. The Tanh model, shown in blue, begins at roughly 48 accuracy and exhibits a gradual upward trend, reaching approximately 50 by 1500 demonstrations. The ELU model, depicted in light purple, starts at an accuracy of 46 and remains largely stagnant, with minor fluctuations peaking at 47. The LLaMA-2-chat-7B model, indicated by a dashed magenta line, maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points. Notably, the Squared Exponential model consistently surpasses all other models, while the ELU model marginally outperforms the Tanh model beyond 1000 demonstrations. The results suggest that the Squared Exponential approach is uniquely effective in leveraging demonstrations to enhance performance on the BBQ task.
